Economic estimates after the SARS outbreak of 2003 and 2004 suggested that it cost between $30 and $100 billion to the economies of affected states, or roughly $3–10 million per case (Keogh-Brown and Smith 2008). These figures are so high that they attract immediate attention—and governments want to avoid these costs as much as possible.
